issues.description: The problem statement's UML and task description specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the provided solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object (and adds a StudentCount class). This structural mismatch is not reflected in the template and will confuse students about the expected return type and required classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the design consistent: either (A) update the problem statement and template to document and provide the StudentCount type (adjust UML and add StudentCount stub in the template), or (B) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (and remove StudentCount). Prefer option A only if the exercise intends to teach using a wrapper class; otherwise adopt option B to match the current UML and reduce student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (an integer total), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object (class StudentCount) instead of an int. This introduces a new identifier/type (StudentCount) and requires callers to use getValue() to obtain the integer. The mismatch between the expected primitive return type in the problem and the object-based return type in the solution creates a conceptual mapping barrier for students: they will search for a method returning an int as specified by the exercise, but the solution uses a differently named type and accessor, increasing extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type and naming across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents) so it matches the UML and problem description; or (B) If StudentCount is intentionally introduced, update the problem statement and UML to specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): StudentCount and explain the StudentCount abstraction so students are not confused. Prefer option A for minimal cognitive load and clearer mapping to the exercise text.
